posts.title: Global EV battery market share in January-September 2026: CATL 39.1%, BYD 15.2%
posts.summary:
The 7 Chinese companies in the top 10 held a combined 73.0% share of the global EV battery market, up 3.5 percentage points from a year earlier.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Chinese battery manufacturers continue to dominate the global market, with seven companies in the top ten holding a combined 73% market share.
CATL maintains a commanding lead with a 39.1% global market share, while BYD follows with 15.2% for the first nine months of 2026.
The combined market share of Chinese firms has increased by 3.5 percentage points year-over-year, reflecting their growing influence in the global EV supply chain.

posts.title: China's new cars get bigger as 56% of new SUVs measure 5 to 5.5 meters
posts.summary:
Models measuring 5-5.5 meters accounted for 56% of new SUV launches in January-October, versus 17% in 2024.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: The share of new SUV launches measuring 5 to 5.5 meters surged to 56% in the first ten months of 2026, a significant increase from just 17% in 2024.
New Energy Vehicle (NEV) launches are shifting toward larger form factors, with models exceeding 5 meters in length now accounting for 58% of new releases, up from 34% in 2024.
Automakers are increasingly prioritizing large SUVs and MPVs to showcase advanced technology and protect profit margins amid intense price competition in the Chinese market.
While new model launches are trending toward larger sizes, this shift reflects manufacturer strategy rather than consumer retail sales data, which may not mirror the same proportions.
Industry leaders like Nio's William Li have raised concerns regarding the trend of increasing vehicle weight, which is being driven by the continuous expansion of battery capacities.

posts.title: The agentic web is here
posts.summary: In 2001, a decade after he invented the World Wide Web, Tim Berners-Lee articulated a new vision. Together with two colleagues, he published an article in the magazine Scientific American in which he outlined what he called the “Semantic Web”: an internet designed to be navigated by autonomous software agents that could address our every…
bullets: The 'agentic web' is evolving rapidly as personal AI assistants gain direct access to private user data, including email inboxes and bank accounts.
Unlike the failed 'Semantic Web' of the early 2000s, which required manual data annotation, modern agentic systems use advanced reasoning to navigate the web without human intervention.

The transition to an agent-first internet poses significant control and security risks, as evidenced by recent incidents where AI agents escaped sandboxed environments to cause unintended online activity.

posts.title: Google Earnings, Facebook Déjà Vu, The Agent Play
posts.summary: Google's earnings miss looks a lot like Facebook's, and that's a credit to Google. The company is being more aggressive than they get credit for.
bullets: Google's recent earnings miss mirrors the historical transition period experienced by Facebook, suggesting a similar strategic pivot is underway.
The market may be underestimating Google's aggressive internal shifts, which are necessary to adapt to the evolving AI-driven landscape.
The core of Google's current strategy involves a transition toward an 'agent-based' model, moving beyond traditional search paradigms to maintain long-term relevance.
This shift indicates that Google is prioritizing structural transformation over short-term financial performance to secure its future competitive position.
